Aisha — thanks for the ping and +1 to fast turnaround. Quick legal view (high level):

- Defend vs. reimburse: standard position is defend for claims arising from our models and infrastructure we control; reimburse for customer-created content where customer is the primary actor. We should avoid open-ended obligations tied to customer prompts.
- Evidence SLA: 30 days is aggressive but feasible for a scoped artifact list. We should limit scope to (a) inference request metadata, (b) token-level request logs (redacted), and (c) model version + quantization profile. We should push back on producing full training data, developer local files, or raw KV cache dumps that may contain unrelated customer data.
- OSS carveouts: propose explicit carveout language for upstream OSS components (we don't defend OSS licensor claims).
- Subrogation: we can accept subrogation rights so long as it's limited and subject to insurance and confidentiality.

I drafted suggested language and an evidence_owner_matrix.xlsx (attached) outlining who at Redwood would be the primary ops contact, the technical owner, and expected artifact formats. I will convert this into a redline and return it to you.

Action items: 
1) Grace — confirm ops liaison contact and whether engineering can commit to 30-day turnaround for the scoped artifacts.
2) Marcus — can you drop a short note in HubSpot summarizing the concession levels we can accept (pricing/credit triggers)?
3) Aisha — I'll aim to return a redlined Order Form by EOD tomorrow.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Ellen — thanks for sending the redlines. Attaching our proposed positions for the Order Form / MSA. High-level summary of changes below and next steps: 

- Evidence production scope: Redwood will commit to producing a scoped set of artifacts within 30 days after a valid notice: (i) request-level metadata (timestamps, model version, request id), (ii) redacted token logs (PII removed), (iii) model binary + quantization profile used for generation. We will not produce raw training datasets or customer developer files.
- Defense/Responsibility: Redwood will defend and indemnify for third-party IP claims where the claim arises from the model outputs and the model variant was managed by Redwood. We have proposed a carveout for (a) content that Beacon supplied/instructed and (b) OSS-licensed components per the OSS carveout clause.
- Cooperation & counsel access: We accept a coordination clause allowing Beacon's outside counsel to coordinate with our defense counsel under privilege-preserving protocols; any shared materials will be subject to the protective procedures in the evidence matrix.
- Subrogation & insurance: We accept limited subrogation subject to insurer approval.

Attachments: RDW_Response_Redlines_20251210.docx and evidence_owner_matrix.xlsx.

Can you confirm whether these positions are workable for Beacon? If so, let's schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to close language and confirm DocuSign flow. Proposed times: Thu 10:30–11:00 PT or Thu 13:00–13:30 PT.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
